tara_customer: Hey @anna_support — customer (Acme Editor extension) hit a case where streaming completions stop mid-response and they got billed for the whole token stream. request-id=req_0b3f7c, region=us-west. They say client shows a brief penultimate chunk then connection closes. billing spike reported. Any ideas?

anna_support: sorry to hear that. do you have a raw curl/http example we can repro with? also paste the gateway logs if possible.

tara_customer: here's the minimal repro they used from the extension (they proxy through an internal relay):

```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \\n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \\n  -d $'--chunk
prompt=hello' \\n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=x-large
```

They attached the gateway snippet: `gateway.log` shows: 
```
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] req=req_0b3f7c upstream=200 written=1024 status=200
[2026-03-10T14:12:15Z] req=req_0b3f7c client_fin received midstream, upstream still sending
[2026-03-10T14:12:15Z] req=req_0b3f7c classify=5xx reason=client_reset_billing_counted
```

deploy-bot: Incident alert: streaming-errors surge +14% (p95 latency up). linked traces: /traces/5201234567

jordan_sre: my 1st pass: looks like the client (extension relay) sends a FIN/halfclose after it got the chunked completion event, but our edge recorded that as a gateway 5xx because we saw `RST` from the proxy layer before the stream completion handshake finished. we should capture tcpdump around req_0b3f7c to confirm TLS/TCP state. can @mike_runtime grab proxy logs + tcpdump?

mike_runtime: grabbing proxy logs now. quick thought — if the relay aggressively closes the client socket on final chunk ack, and our response pipeline tries to write a trailing chunk (or keepalive), the kernel can return `EPIPE` which our metrics classifier currently maps to gateway 502 and we bill. i can repro with a small python server that halfcloses after flush.

mike_runtime: repro command I used:
```
# start small server that flushes then close client immediately
python -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 &
# then simulate relay that halfcloses after first data
(echo -e "POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n5\r\nhello\r\n0\r\n\r\n"; sleep 0.1; kill -9 $SERVER_PID) | nc localhost 8000
```

anna_support: ok can you paste the gateway trace fields where we mark the request as 5xx? what classifier matched?

mike_runtime: classifier: `client_socket_teardown_midstream` (current mapping -> 502). trace shows upstream wrote last chunk at 14:12:14.880, kernel write returned EPIPE at 14:12:15.001, client FIN at 14:12:15.002, classifier fired and billing flagged tokens billed 100%.

jordan_sre: two followups: 1) we should treat `EPIPE`/client-halfclose differently when the upstream has already emitted terminal chunk(s) — treat as success (499-like) for billing. 2) need to confirm the relay behaviour — is it sending `FIN` before reading server trailing data? could be a bug in their netstack. request we get a pcap.

billing_ops: hold any charge adjustments until we confirm root cause. if we change classification we need a clear retroactive rule for tokens billed. please add timeline and affected accounts.

anna_support: tara, can you ask Acme for a pcap + exact extension version and whether they use http1.1 keepalive reuse? also ask them to try curl --no-buffer (above) and `--http1.1` to see if it changes.

tara_customer: sent pcap to eng@, extension v2.3.1, they confirm relay reuses connection pool to edge and aggressively closes the client side after seeing their own UI acknowledge. attached pcap id=pcap_5201234567.

mike_runtime: notes for fix: short-term: update classifier to map `client_socket_teardown_midstream` -> non-billing if upstream last-write timestamp >= (now - 200ms) and response included final-chunk marker. I'll open a small patch and run canary. long-term: make streaming ACK handshake stronger + add explicit server-side trailing frame before counting billable completion.

anna_support: thanks. I'll coordinate customer comms once we have canary and a billing decision. tagging @billing_ops for timeline. :thumbsup:

billing_ops: thanks — please add a list of request-ids + tokens for the last 48h pinned to the ticket. we'll tentatively freeze billing for affected accounts until root cause validated.

jordan_sre: next steps: (1) mike deploys classifier patch to canary in us-west, (2) run replay against pcap_5201234567, (3) if repro -> flip classification and run small backfill to detect scope. I'll own rollout plan.

anna_support: copying summary into the support ticket and will reply to Acme saying we're investigating and may issue credits. will update here when canary is up.

tara_customer: thanks team. I'll keep customer updated.
